newsitem.title: USA: First Montauk expects higher revs.
newsitem.headline: First Montauk expects higher revs.

text.p: First Montauk Financial Corp said it expects to report revenues of about $36.1 million for 1996, up about 27 percent from $28.3 million in 1995.

For the 1996 fourth quarter, the company expects revenues of nearly $9 million, an increase from $8.3 million in the comparable prior year quarter and $7.1 million reported in the immediately preceding third quarter of 1996.

The company said its higher revenues, coupled with controlled expenses, would have allowed it to report increased operating income compared to the year before. However, results of operations were hurt by costs to settle securities claims arising from the actions of a former branch office.

Legal and settlement costs for 1996 totaled about $2.3 million, including charges of $1.3 million in the fourth quarter. The company said it is discussing with insurers the extent of coverage for certain legal claims.

Exclusive of legal and settlement costs, the company would have reported a pretax profit of about $2.9 million for the fiscal 1996 or $0.20 per share after tax, and a $720,000 pretax profit or $0.05 per share after-tax for the quarter ended December 31, 1996. Inclusive of legal and settlement costs incurred during the fourth quarter of 1996 of approximately $1.3 million, a charge of about $.09 per share after-tax, the company expects to report an after-tax loss for this period of $340,000, or $0.04 per share. The fiscal 1996 after-tax profit should about $360,000 or $0.04 per share.
The company said the 1996 figures are estimates. Audited financial results on Form 10-K will be available by March 31.
